question.knowledge_point: Identifying a Vertically Shifted Exponential Decay Curve
question.problem: Which of the following is the graph of  $y={(\frac{1}{10})}^{x}-\frac{1}{10}?$
question.worked_solution:
First we plot the graph of $y={(\frac{1}{10})}^{x}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/f02afa6dd2d1c107fd72b1221fddb7f6c698506deb834cad0dc11af1bebb18e6.png)

Next, we shift this graph $\frac{1}{10}$ units down. 
The horizontal asymptote under such a transformation becomes $y=-\frac{1}{10},$ the $y$-intercept becomes $(0,\frac{9}{10}).$
The resulting graph of $y={(\frac{1}{10})}^{x}-\frac{1}{10}$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/57539870ff45bae449d3ad7c11580d9c8068cfe76ac98c2f849ee38494288036.png)
